h1: AI UGC Videos for Food and Beverage Products
lead: Upload the citrus bottle and let an AI avatar pour it over ice for an AI UGC video. You get a clip you can post, without booking a kitchen for the pour.

faq.q: Will the ingredient list and nutrition panel look right?
faq.a: Do not rely on the image for small print. Allergens, ingredients, and nutrition facts should always come from the real label.

faq.q: Can I turn a bottle photo into a pour video?
faq.a: Yes. Upload the citrus bottle or paste a product link, then describe the glass, the ice, and the color of the liquid. Name the texture in plain words so the pour stays close to the real drink.

faq.q: How long should a food clip be, and what does it cost?
faq.a: A 6-second pour is 24 credits, and 6 or 10 seconds covers one pour or one bite. Use 15 seconds for two moments, or 30 seconds for a longer serve. 10 seconds is 40 credits, 15 is 60, and 30 is 120. A still image is 24 credits. A failed job returns its credits. Starter is $24.50 a month for 200 credits, Pro is $35 for 300, and Premium is $63 for 600.

faq.q: Should I spray the bottle so it looks cold?
faq.a: No. Ask for condensation in the description, then photograph the dry bottle in side window light with fingerprints wiped off.

faq.q: Can I run the clips as paid food and drink ads?
faq.a: Yes. The download has no watermark, and you can use it in paid ads.

faq.q: Do I need a creator or a filming kitchen?
faq.a: Not for these clips. Pick an AI avatar, or let the hands come from your bottle photo. A real tasting, or a recipe you must show exactly, still needs a real shoot.

faq.q: Which video shapes can I use?
faq.a: Use 9:16 for a phone feed, 1:1 for a square, 16:9 for a wide page, and 4:3 or 3:4 when the page asks for them. A square photo fits many listings.

faq.q: What should the scene keep visible?
faq.a: Keep the package shape and the main label area recognizable, and end on the full product when you can. Do not ask the clip to invent a flavor that is not in the photo.

faq.q: Can a drink ad include a voice, captions, and another language?
faq.a: Yes. The clip can include a spoken line and captions, and the same pour can be made again in another language.
